claims.text: A high-dimensional machine-learning potential trained exclusively on DFT data from solid and liquid configurations near melting will reproduce local atomic environments in multicomponent refractory HEAs more accurately than traditional EAM references.
More accurate reproduction of local environments by the machine-learning potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method targets quinary or higher-order refractory HEAs such as HfNbTaTiZr in both solid and liquid states.
The applicable near-melting temperature range is approximately 2000–2500 K.
The machine-learning potential should be trained on an extensive set of ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots spanning the solid-to-liquid transition.
The relevant configuration space includes ordered solid environments and disordered liquid environments over the near-melting temperature range.
Traditional EAM potentials fail to capture local heterogeneity in refractory HEAs.
A DFT-trained machine-learning potential can bridge the gap between classical-reference and DFT phase spaces by reproducing DFT local chemical environments and interactions.
Training on diverse high-temperature DFT configurations will capture variations in local coordination and bonding that EAM potentials miss.
Improved representation of coordination and bonding will produce a smoother thermodynamic-integration path.
A smoother integration path will produce more accurate free-energy estimates.
Machine-learning-reference free energies will agree more closely with all-DFT or direct ab initio MD results than free energies obtained using TOR-TILD EAM references.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the many configurations of the ab initio liquid.
Poor phase-space overlap from TOR-TILD's EAM references leads to larger free-energy integration errors.
The method's validity is expected to be limited to high-melting multicomponent refractory HEAs unless it is separately demonstrated for other bonding regimes.
Application to low-melting alloys or alloys with markedly different bonding may require re-parameterization or different training data.
Long ab initio MD simulations lasting tens to hundreds of picoseconds can provide a converged free-energy benchmark for the comparison.
Failure to reduce path-mismatch error by at least 50% relative to the EAM approach will falsify the hypothesis.
